product_scope.problem_statement: The current repository was assembled iteratively and cannot be assumed to satisfy the challenge end-to-end. Before reimplementation begins, the team needs a factual diagnosis of what is usable, what is risky, and what is missing.
product_scope.goal: Produce a repository audit that classifies the current implementation, identifies gaps against the challenge, and defines the baseline architecture and roadmap for phased reimplementation.
success_outcomes: Every major area of the current repository is classified as keep, refactor, or discard.
A concrete list of challenge gaps is documented against the current implementation.
The team has a defendable decision on what architecture will serve as the baseline for reimplementation.
The next phases can start from a shared factual diagnosis instead of assumptions.

in_scope: Audit of current source structure, infrastructure code, and tests.
Comparison of the current repository against the challenge requirements in goal.txt.
Classification of current modules into keep, refactor, or discard.
Identification of architectural inconsistencies, missing guarantees, and weak assumptions.
Definition of the phased roadmap and reimplementation baseline.
out_of_scope: Editing runtime code to fix the application in this phase.
Expanding infrastructure beyond what is needed to support the diagnosis.
Writing final production documentation for all later phases.

actors.name: Technical Reviewer
actors.description: Needs a clear diagnosis of the repository before trusting any implementation path.

actors.name: Implementation Team
actors.description: Uses the audit to decide what to rebuild and in what order.

user_journeys.name: Diagnose the current repository
steps: The team reads the repository and challenge objective.
The team compares current behavior and architecture against the target requirements.
The team documents what is solid, what is partial, and what is misleading.

user_journeys.name: Choose the reimplementation baseline
steps: The team reviews the audit output.
The team decides which modules are worth preserving as building blocks.
The team defines the baseline architecture for the next implementation phases.

use_cases.title: Audit source modules
use_cases.description: Review handlers, domain logic, adapters, and shared types to determine if they align with the challenge.

use_cases.title: Audit infrastructure code
use_cases.description: Review CDK resources and wiring to determine whether the infrastructure matches the runtime design and challenge requirements.

use_cases.title: Audit test coverage quality
use_cases.description: Determine whether existing tests prove real challenge guarantees or only local behavior.

use_cases.title: Define reimplementation baseline
use_cases.description: Establish the architecture and work phases that will be used going forward.

business_rules.rule: The current repository must not be treated as correct by default.
A module can only be preserved if it is both technically sound and compatible with the target architecture.
Tests that pass do not prove challenge completeness unless they validate required system guarantees.
The audit must identify gaps against goal.txt explicitly, not implicitly.
This phase must produce a baseline for future specs, not implementation changes.

functional_requirements.title: Repository classification
functional_requirements.statement: The audit must classify the main modules and assets into keep, refactor, or discard.

functional_requirements.title: Challenge gap analysis
functional_requirements.statement: The audit must document which challenge requirements are fully covered, partially covered, or not covered.

functional_requirements.title: Architecture baseline
functional_requirements.statement: The audit must define the architecture baseline that later phases will implement or refine.

functional_requirements.title: Phased roadmap
functional_requirements.statement: The audit must produce a phased roadmap aligned with the spec-driven workflow.

acceptance_criteria.given: The repository contains application code, infrastructure code, and tests
acceptance_criteria.then: Each major repository area is explicitly classified as keep, refactor, or discard.

acceptance_criteria.given: The challenge defines mandatory architecture and operational goals
acceptance_criteria.when: The audit compares the current repository against goal.txt
acceptance_criteria.then: The resulting diagnosis states which requirements are covered, partially covered, or missing.

acceptance_criteria.given: The team must reimplement the solution in phases
acceptance_criteria.then: A phased roadmap and baseline architecture are documented for the next specs.
They improve decision quality without changing the runtime implementation.

assumptions: The repository builds and current unit tests passing are useful signals, but not proof of end-to-end challenge fitness.
The challenge will be judged on architecture quality and defendable tradeoffs, not only on the presence of AWS services.
The next implementation phase should optimize for a correct and explainable core flow before advanced scaling patterns.

open_questions.question: Which current modules are efficient enough to keep without compromising clarity in later phases?
Which scaling patterns must be fully implemented versus clearly scaffolded in later phases?
